experiment.steer: S015 §113 a learned performance model; §15 Kernel Forge priors

headline: §113's model 'in the sense of something that GENERALISES across primitives' was named NOT BUILT by the perf-model receipt. Built and tested here, and the result splits: the DIRECTION generalises and the MAGNITUDE does not. THE OCCUPANCY CLIFF IS NOT AT A FIXED per_tg -- it sits where threadgroup dispatch overtakes the primitive's own work, so a CHEAPER kernel is still 1.90x off its floor exactly where the fused chain has already flattened.

the_model_written_before_the_run.form: time(per_tg) = max(T, threadgroups / R), T the primitive's saturated time, R a machine constant
the_model_written_before_the_run.why_it_could_generalise: if R is a property of the machine and T of the primitive, one fit predicts every other primitive's cliff without measuring it
the_model_written_before_the_run.additive_form_considered_and_rejected_on: time = T + tg/R gives R = 1.18e9 and 3.11e9 at the two cliff points, 2.6x apart, while max() gives 5.49e8 and 4.39e8, 1.25x apart. The worse model was not carried forward.

the_prediction_and_the_verdict.chain_is_the_fit_not_a_test: chain's 74.9 is self-fit and proves nothing
the_prediction_and_the_verdict.verdict: DIRECTION CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE REFUTED. Both OUT-OF-SAMPLE predictions miss by about 2x AND IN THE SAME DIRECTION -- write-only predicted 128 and degrades out to 256, heavy predicted no cliff above 15 and still pays 1.15x at 32. A model that is wrong twice the same way is wrong about its SHAPE, not unlucky.
the_prediction_and_the_verdict.what_the_same_sign_points_at: max() predicts a KNEE -- exactly at floor above per_tg*. The write-only curve is 2.94 / 1.90 / 1.37 / 1.11 / 1.02, a SMOOTH DECAY, so the transition is gradual and the bad region reaches further than any hard-corner model allows.
the_prediction_and_the_verdict.the_fixed_per_threadgroup_cost_model_die: excess over floor for write-only is 0.5764 / 0.2685 / 0.1092 / 0.0305 / 0.0044 ms against threadgroup counts halving each step; successive ratios 2.15, 2.46, 3.58, 6.9 where a fixed cost per threadgroup demands a flat 2.0. Both simple models fail and a third fitted to five points would be curve-fitting, so none is claimed.

the_measured_landscapes.read_it_as: three primitives, three different answers about the same machine. write-only is 1.90x off at per_tg 64 where the chain is 1.17x and the heavy kernel 1.05x.

per_tg_is_the_variable_and_now_it_is_a_r.why_it_had_to_be_redone: the perf-model receipt rested this on ONE pair. The sweep here varies threadgroup size and per_tg together below 256, so it cannot tell them apart on its own -- reading a second primitive's sweep without settling that would have been reading a confound.
per_tg_is_the_variable_and_now_it_is_a_r.the_decisive_part_is_what_does_NOT_track: those four differ 8x IN THREAD COUNT -- 2.1M against 16.7M -- and land within 1.88%. Thread count is ruled out; threadgroup COUNT is what tracks.
per_tg_is_the_variable_and_now_it_is_a_r.AND_THE_COLLAPSE_HAS_A_MEASURED_EXCEPTIO: on the READ-heavy chain an ept of 8 costs 7.9% at per_tg 256 and 7.6% at 512 against the same per_tg reached with a larger threadgroup, while the write-only kernel shows no such penalty (1.88% and 0.17%). per_tg is dominant, NOT total -- so candidates sharing it are not deduped, only reported as the near-duplicates they are.
per_tg_is_the_variable_and_now_it_is_a_r.noise_caveat_stated_not_buried: five write-only arms near the floor carry 10.0-11.5% IQR, ABOVE the 10% gate, and the 1.88% collapse spread is well INSIDE that. So the collapse establishes that NO LARGE effect of the split exists -- it does not establish agreement to 1.88%. The 8x-thread-count conclusion survives because an effect of that size could not hide under 11% noise.

what_this_corrects_in_the_forge.the_claim_being_corrected: ACCELERATOR_PERF_MODEL.json recorded 'THREADGROUP_PRIOR stops at 64 and that exclusion is now MEASURED rather than assumed'. True, and measured ON ONE PRIMITIVE.
what_this_corrects_in_the_forge.why_that_matters_concretely: the prior's grid STARTS at threadgroup 64. For a write-only kernel per_tg 64/128/256 are 1.90x / 1.37x / 1.11x off the floor, so a search that trusted this prior as a machine property would spend its whole budget inside another primitive's bad region and crown a champion 1.9x off the achievable floor.
shipped: Candidate.per_tg, the variable that actually tracks time
collapse_groups(): the default 15-candidate grid covers only 7 distinct per_tg values, so roughly half the search re-measures a point it already holds
the prior's comment now carries the three-primitive table and says CHAIN-SHAPED PRIOR, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE MACHINE
two tests, one pinning the 15-to-7 redundancy and one pinning the caveat in source
what_this_corrects_in_the_forge.NOT_shipped_and_why: the candidates are not deduped by per_tg, because the collapse has a measured 7.9% exception on read-heavy kernels at ept 8; discarding a candidate that can differ by 7.9% to save reps would be trading a real measurement for a convenient assumption.

reproducibility.means: the landscape the prior was fit on reproduces across processes and days to 0.4%

claim_boundary.correctness_first: all three kernels verified against a numpy oracle before timing -- write-only 0.0, chain 9.54e-07, heavy checked finite and not the input
claim_boundary.one_shape: n = 2^24 f32 only; nothing here says how the cliff moves with n
claim_boundary.one_machine: INSTANCE. 60 GPU cores, one M3 Ultra, not promoted
claim_boundary.heavy_is_latency_bound_not_throughput_bo: its 256 FMAs are a serial dependent chain at ~1.7 TFLOP/s, well under peak, so it stands in for EXPENSIVE PER ELEMENT and not for a tuned compute-bound kernel
claim_boundary.no_champion_moves: no existing forge result changes; what changes is how far its prior travels
claim_boundary.the_generalising_model_is_still_not_buil: what exists is a DIRECTIONAL rule -- cheaper primitive, cliff reaches further -- which tells a search WHERE TO LOOK and cannot tell it what it will find. §113's model in the strong sense remains unbuilt and is not claimed.
